{"questions": [
{
"id": "p1",
"topic": "combinatorics: subsets, partitions and selections (difference of binomial coefficients, factor pairs)",
"error_type": "omitted_case",
"question": "Find the sum of the positive integers n for which there exists a positive integer m < n such that a set with n elements has exactly 45 more two-element subsets than a set with m elements.",
"answer": 120,
"target_wrong": 110,
"error_description": "The factor pair (9, 10) of 90 gives n − m = 9, n + m − 1 = 10, i.e. n = 10, m = 1; it is dropped because a 1-element set has 0 two-element subsets and looks like a non-case. Omitting it gives 120 − 10 = 110.",
"cases": ["(1,90): n=46, m=45", "(2,45): n=24, m=22", "(3,30): n=17, m=14", "(5,18): n=12, m=7", "(6,15): n=11, m=5", "(9,10): n=10, m=1"],
"solution": "We need C(n,2) − C(m,2) = 45, i.e. n(n−1) − m(m−1) = 90, which factors as (n − m)(n + m − 1) = 90. Since n − m < n + m − 1 and the two factors have opposite parity (their sum is 2n − 1), we list factor pairs d·e = 90 with d < e: (1,90), (2,45), (3,30), (5,18), (6,15), (9,10); all have opposite parity. From n = (d + e + 1)/2 and m = (e − d + 1)/2 we get (n,m) = (46,45), (24,22), (17,14), (12,7), (11,5), (10,1). Each has 1 ≤ m < n (the last one works since a 1-element set has 0 two-element subsets and C(10,2) = 45). The sum of the n's is 46 + 24 + 17 + 12 + 11 + 10 = 120.",
"check_code": "from math import comb\ntotal = 0\nfor n in range(2, 500):\n    if any(comb(n, 2) - comb(m, 2) == 45 for m in range(1, n)):\n        total += n\nprint(total)"
},
{
"id": "p2",
"topic": "combinatorics: subsets, partitions and selections (3-element subsets forming geometric progressions)",
"error_type": "omitted_case",
"question": "How many 3-element subsets of {1, 2, …, 30} have the property that their elements, listed in increasing order, form a geometric progression?",
"answer": 19,
"target_wrong": 18,
"error_description": "The common ratio 5/3, giving the single subset {9, 15, 25}, is omitted; the list of ratios 2, 3, 3/2, 4, 4/3, 5, 5/2, 5/4 looks complete. This gives 18 instead of 19.",
"cases": ["ratio 2: a,2a,4a with a≤7 (7 subsets)", "ratio 3: a,3a,9a with a≤3 (3)", "ratio 3/2: 4k,6k,9k with k≤3 (3)", "ratio 4: {1,4,16} (1)", "ratio 4/3: {9,12,16} (1)", "ratio 5: {1,5,25} (1)", "ratio 5/2: {4,10,25} (1)", "ratio 5/3: {9,15,25} (1)", "ratio 5/4: {16,20,25} (1)"],
"solution": "Write the common ratio in lowest terms as p/q with p > q ≥ 1. Then the progression is q²k, pqk, p²k for a positive integer k, and we need p²k ≤ 30, so p ≤ 5. p=2,q=1: k ≤ 7, 7 subsets. p=3,q=1: 9k ≤ 30, k ≤ 3, 3 subsets. p=3,q=2: 9k ≤ 30, 3 subsets. p=4,q=1: 16k ≤ 30, k=1, 1 subset. p=4,q=3: 1 subset ({9,12,16}). p=5,q=1: {1,5,25}. p=5,q=2: {4,10,25}. p=5,q=3: {9,15,25}. p=5,q=4: {16,20,25}. Total 7+3+3+1+1+1+1+1+1 = 19.",
"check_code": "from itertools import combinations\nprint(sum(1 for a, b, c in combinations(range(1, 31), 3) if b * b == a * c))"
},
{
"id": "p3",
"topic": "combinatorics: subsets, partitions and selections (set partitions with restricted block sizes)",
"error_type": "omitted_case",
"question": "In how many ways can a class of 12 students be divided into study groups so that every group has exactly 2, 3, or 4 students? (The groups are not labeled; two divisions are the same if they consist of the same groups.)",
"answer": 412720,
"target_wrong": 360745,
"error_description": "The size pattern 4+4+2+2 (contributing 12!/(4!·4!·2!·2!·2!·2!) = 51975) is left out of the list of partitions of 12 into parts 2, 3, 4; the remaining six patterns sum to 360745.",
"cases": ["4+4+4: 5775", "4+4+2+2: 51975", "4+3+3+2: 138600", "4+2+2+2+2: 51975", "3+3+3+3: 15400", "3+3+2+2+2: 138600", "2+2+2+2+2+2: 10395"],
"solution": "The multiset of group sizes is a partition of 12 into parts from {2,3,4}: 4+4+4, 4+4+2+2, 4+3+3+2, 4+2+2+2+2, 3+3+3+3, 3+3+2+2+2, 2+2+2+2+2+2. For a pattern with sizes s_i where size s occurs m_s times, the number of divisions is 12!/(∏ s_i! · ∏ m_s!). Computing: 4+4+4: 12!/(24³·3!) = 5775. 4+4+2+2: 12!/(24²·2²·2!·2!) = 51975. 4+3+3+2: 12!/(24·6·6·2·2!) = 138600. 4+2+2+2+2: 12!/(24·2⁴·4!) = 51975. 3+3+3+3: 12!/(6⁴·4!) = 15400. 3+3+2+2+2: 12!/(6²·2³·2!·3!) = 138600. 2⁶: 12!/(2⁶·6!) = 10395. Sum: 5775+51975+138600+51975+15400+138600+10395 = 412720. (Check: the recurrence f(n) = (n−1)f(n−2) + C(n−1,2)f(n−3) + C(n−1,3)f(n−4) also gives f(12) = 412720.)",
"check_code": "from itertools import combinations\n\ndef count(rem):\n    if not rem:\n        return 1\n    first, rest = rem[0], rem[1:]\n    t = 0\n    for k in (1, 2, 3):\n        for grp in combinations(rest, k):\n            s = set(grp)\n            t += count(tuple(x for x in rest if x not in s))\n    return t\n\nprint(count(tuple(range(12))))"
},
{
"id": "p4",
"topic": "combinatorics: subsets, partitions and selections (pairs of 2-element subsets with equal sums)",
"error_type": "omitted_case",
"question": "Find the number of unordered pairs {A, B} of disjoint two-element subsets of {1, 2, …, 8} such that the sum of the elements of A equals the sum of the elements of B.",
"answer": 22,
"target_wrong": 21,
"error_description": "The sum 13, achieved by {5,8} and {6,7}, is omitted from the list of sums (the list stops at 12 or skips it), losing 1 pair: 21 instead of 22.",
"cases": ["sum 5: {1,4},{2,3} → 1 pair", "sum 6: {1,5},{2,4} → 1", "sum 7: {1,6},{2,5},{3,4} → 3", "sum 8: {1,7},{2,6},{3,5} → 3", "sum 9: {1,8},{2,7},{3,6},{4,5} → 6", "sum 10: {2,8},{3,7},{4,6} → 3", "sum 11: {3,8},{4,7},{5,6} → 3", "sum 12: {4,8},{5,7} → 1", "sum 13: {5,8},{6,7} → 1"],
"solution": "Two distinct 2-element subsets with the same sum are automatically disjoint (if they shared an element, the other elements would be equal too). So we count, for each possible sum s, the number k_s of 2-element subsets with sum s, and add C(k_s, 2). The counts are: s=3:1, 4:1, 5:2, 6:2, 7:3, 8:3, 9:4, 10:3, 11:3, 12:2, 13:2, 14:1, 15:1. Thus the answer is C(2,2)+C(2,2)+C(3,2)+C(3,2)+C(4,2)+C(3,2)+C(3,2)+C(2,2)+C(2,2) = 1+1+3+3+6+3+3+1+1 = 22.",
"check_code": "from itertools import combinations\npairs = list(combinations(range(1, 9), 2))\ncnt = 0\nfor A, B in combinations(pairs, 2):\n    if not set(A) & set(B) and sum(A) == sum(B):\n        cnt += 1\nprint(cnt)"
},
{
"id": "p5",
"topic": "combinatorics: subsets, partitions and selections (partition of a set into two equal-sum parts)",
"error_type": "omitted_case",
"question": "In how many ways can the set {1, 2, …, 8} be partitioned into two nonempty subsets so that the sum of the elements in one subset equals the sum of the elements in the other?",
"answer": 7,
"target_wrong": 6,
"error_description": "The partition {1,2,3,4,8} | {5,6,7}, where the part containing 8 has five elements, is omitted (the enumeration stops after parts of size 3 and 4). This gives 6 instead of 7.",
"cases": ["{3,7,8} | {1,2,4,5,6}", "{4,6,8} | {1,2,3,5,7}", "{1,2,7,8} | {3,4,5,6}", "{1,3,6,8} | {2,4,5,7}", "{1,4,5,8} | {2,3,6,7}", "{2,3,5,8} | {1,4,6,7}", "{1,2,3,4,8} | {5,6,7}"],
"solution": "The total 1+2+…+8 = 36, so each part must sum to 18. Each partition is determined by the part containing 8, which is a subset of {1,…,7} with sum 10 together with 8. Subsets of {1,…,7} summing to 10: size 2: {3,7}, {4,6}; size 3: {1,2,7}, {1,3,6}, {1,4,5}, {2,3,5}; size 4: {1,2,3,4}; size 1 or ≥5 is impossible (max of 4 smallest is 10 exactly, 5 smallest sum to 15). That is 2+4+1 = 7 subsets, hence 7 partitions.",
"check_code": "from itertools import combinations\nS = range(1, 9)\ntotal = sum(S)\ncnt = 0\nfor r in range(1, 8):\n    for sub in combinations(S, r):\n        if 8 in sub and 2 * sum(sub) == total:\n            cnt += 1\nprint(cnt)"
},
{
"id": "p6",
"topic": "combinatorics: subsets, partitions and selections (3-element subsets satisfying the triangle inequality)",
"error_type": "omitted_case",
"question": "Let P be the set of prime numbers less than 20. How many 3-element subsets of P consist of three numbers that can be the side lengths of a non-degenerate triangle?",
"answer": 16,
"target_wrong": 15,
"error_description": "In the case largest side 19, the subset {3,17,19} (3+17 = 20 > 19, barely) is omitted, giving 6 instead of 7 for that case and 15 overall.",
"cases": ["largest 5: none", "largest 7: {3,5,7}", "largest 11: {5,7,11}", "largest 13: {3,11,13},{5,11,13},{7,11,13}", "largest 17: {5,13,17},{7,11,17},{7,13,17},{11,13,17}", "largest 19: {3,17,19},{5,17,19},{7,13,19},{7,17,19},{11,13,19},{11,17,19},{13,17,19}"],
"solution": "P = {2,3,5,7,11,13,17,19}. For a < b < c the triangle condition is a + b > c. Side 2 can never be used, since 2 + b > c with b < c primes forces c = b + 1, impossible for odd primes b ≥ 3. Casework on the largest side c: c=5: {2,3} fails. c=7: only {3,5}: 1. c=11: need a+b > 11 from {3,5,7}: only {5,7}: 1. c=13: from {3,5,7,11}: {3,11},{5,11},{7,11}: 3. c=17: from {3,…,13}: {5,13},{7,11},{7,13},{11,13}: 4. c=19: from {3,…,17}: {3,17},{5,17},{7,13},{7,17},{11,13},{11,17},{13,17}: 7. Total 1+1+3+4+7 = 16.",
"check_code": "from itertools import combinations\nprimes = [p for p in range(2, 20) if all(p % d for d in range(2, p))]\nprint(sum(1 for a, b, c in combinations(primes, 3) if a + b > c))"
},
{
"id": "p7",
"topic": "combinatorics: subsets, partitions and selections (sum of products over 3-element subsets)",
"error_type": "algebra_slip",
"question": "For every 3-element subset of {1, 2, …, 8}, compute the product of its three elements. Find the sum of these products taken over all 3-element subsets.",
"answer": 4536,
"target_wrong": 3672,
"error_description": "A sign slip in Newton's identity: using e3 = (p1³ − 3p1p2 − 2p3)/6 instead of (p1³ − 3p1p2 + 2p3)/6, giving (46656 − 22032 − 2592)/6 = 3672 instead of 4536.",
"cases": [],
"solution": "The required sum is the elementary symmetric polynomial e3(1,2,…,8). With power sums p1 = 1+…+8 = 36, p2 = 1²+…+8² = 204, p3 = 1³+…+8³ = 36² = 1296, Newton's identity gives e3 = (p1³ − 3p1p2 + 2p3)/6 = (46656 − 22032 + 2592)/6 = 27216/6 = 4536. (Check: e3(1,…,n) equals the unsigned Stirling number c(n+1, n−2) = C(n+1,2)·C(n+1,4); for n=8 this is 36·126 = 4536.)",
"check_code": "from itertools import combinations\nprint(sum(a * b * c for a, b, c in combinations(range(1, 9), 3)))"
},
{
"id": "p8",
"topic": "combinatorics: subsets, partitions and selections (subsets with a parity count condition)",
"error_type": "misread_condition",
"question": "How many 7-element subsets of {1, 2, …, 14} contain at least five odd numbers?",
"answer": 491,
"target_wrong": 441,
"error_description": "Reading 'at least five odd numbers' as 'exactly five odd numbers' and computing only C(7,5)·C(7,2) = 441, dropping the six-odd and seven-odd cases (49 + 1).",
"cases": [],
"solution": "The set has 7 odd numbers and 7 even numbers. A 7-element subset with exactly k odd numbers can be chosen in C(7,k)·C(7,7−k) ways. For k = 5, 6, 7: C(7,5)·C(7,2) = 21·21 = 441; C(7,6)·C(7,1) = 7·7 = 49; C(7,7)·C(7,0) = 1. Total 441 + 49 + 1 = 491.",
"check_code": "from itertools import combinations\nprint(sum(1 for s in combinations(range(1, 15), 7) if sum(x % 2 for x in s) >= 5))"
},
{
"id": "p9",
"topic": "combinatorics: subsets, partitions and selections (subsets containing at least two special elements)",
"error_type": "double_counting",
"question": "How many 5-element subsets of {1, 2, …, 15} contain at least two perfect squares?",
"answer": 726,
"target_wrong": 858,
"error_description": "Choosing two of the three squares (C(3,2) = 3) and then any 3 of the remaining 13 numbers, C(13,3) = 286, giving 858; subsets containing all three squares are counted three times instead of once.",
"cases": [],
"solution": "The perfect squares in {1,…,15} are 1, 4, 9, so there are 3 squares and 12 non-squares. Count by the exact number of squares: exactly two: C(3,2)·C(12,3) = 3·220 = 660; exactly three: C(3,3)·C(12,2) = 66. Total 660 + 66 = 726.",
"check_code": "from itertools import combinations\nsq = {1, 4, 9}\nprint(sum(1 for s in combinations(range(1, 16), 5) if len(sq & set(s)) >= 2))"
},
{
"id": "p10",
"topic": "combinatorics: subsets, partitions and selections (3-element subsets with bounded spread)",
"error_type": "off_by_one",
"question": "How many 3-element subsets {a, b, c} of {1, 2, …, 30} with a < b < c satisfy c − a ≤ 10?",
"answer": 1020,
"target_wrong": 840,
"error_description": "Treating the condition c − a ≤ 10 as strict (c − a < 10), so the spread d = 10 case, contributing (30 − 10)·9 = 180 subsets, is excluded: 840 instead of 1020.",
"cases": [],
"solution": "Let d = c − a, where 2 ≤ d ≤ 10. For a fixed d, a can be any of 1, …, 30 − d (so that c = a + d ≤ 30), and b can be any of the d − 1 integers strictly between a and c. Hence the count is Σ_{d=2}^{10} (30 − d)(d − 1) = 28·1 + 27·2 + 26·3 + 25·4 + 24·5 + 23·6 + 22·7 + 21·8 + 20·9 = 28 + 54 + 78 + 100 + 120 + 138 + 154 + 168 + 180 = 1020.",
"check_code": "from itertools import combinations\nprint(sum(1 for a, b, c in combinations(range(1, 31), 3) if c - a <= 10))"
}
]}
